<!-- slide 14 -->
# Time Series Plots {.divider}

[Trajectories with uncertainty]{.eyebrow}


<!-- slide 15 -->
## What Is a Time Series Plot? {.smaller}

[Time series · theory]{.eyebrow}

### x is time, y is the measurement, lines show trends, bars or bands show uncertainty

A **time series plot** answers two questions at once: *what is the trajectory*, and *how confident are we at each point*. The x-axis carries time (minutes, hours, days, weeks), the y-axis carries the measurement (expression, abundance, signal). One **line per entity** traces its trajectory — gene, sample, cell line, patient.

The interesting question is always **how to show uncertainty** around each point:

- **Error bars** (`ax.errorbar`): vertical whiskers ± SEM or 95% CI at every measured time. Best when you have **few points** (≤ 6 timepoints) — the eye can read each whisker.
- **Ribbons** (`ax.fill_between`): a translucent band between mean ± SEM. Best when you have **many points** (a dense kinetic curve) — error bars would clutter; a ribbon shows the envelope at a glance.
- **Small multiples**: one panel per entity, faint grey context behind each focal trajectory. Best when you have **many entities** and lines overlap.

The rule is: pick the encoding that lets the audience *read direction + confidence* without effort.


<!-- slide 16 -->
## Time Series · The Data {.smaller}

[Time series · data peek]{.eyebrow}

### One row per (gene, timepoint) — tpm with its standard error

`load_timecourse()` returns a tidy long-form table: 6 genes (BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, MYC, KRAS, PTEN) measured at 5 timepoints (0, 2, 6, 12, 24 hours), with the mean **tpm** and its standard error **sem**. Long-form is the format every plotting library expects.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

tc = load_timecourse()           # gene, time, tpm, sem  (long-form, 6 genes x 5 timepoints)
tc.head(6)
```


<!-- slide 17 -->
## Time Series · The `.sem` Footgun {.smaller}

[Time series · gotcha]{.eyebrow}

### `DataFrame.sem` is a *method*. Always use bracket access for the column

This dataset has a column literally called `sem` — the standard error of the mean. **But** pandas DataFrames already have a `.sem()` *method* (it computes the standard error). Dot access loses to the method every time and you get a confusing error. The fix is one character: brackets.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**The bug** — `tc.sem` returns the **method**, not the column:

```python
tc = load_timecourse()

tc.sem                       # bound method, not data
# <bound method ... DataFrame.sem of ...>

tc.sem.values                # AttributeError!
# AttributeError: 'function' object
#  has no attribute 'values'
```

When you pass `yerr=tc.sem` to matplotlib you get a cryptic `TypeError` because matplotlib tried to use the method as an array.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**The fix** — always use bracket access:

```python
tc = load_timecourse()

tc["sem"]                    # the actual column
# 0    3.062
# 1    1.901
# ...

tc["sem"].values             # plain numpy array
# array([3.06, 1.90, 2.32, ...])
```

**Rule of thumb**: prefer `df["col"]` over `df.col` *always*. Brackets work for every legal name; dots silently break on `mean`, `sum`, `sem`, `count`, `index`, `T`, …
:::
::::

## Time Series · Step 1 — One Gene {.smaller}

[Time series · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · BRCA1 only, time vs tpm

Build the **idea** on one gene. Filter the long table to BRCA1, draw time on x and tpm on y. A single `ax.plot` with markers tells the trajectory.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1-2|4-5|7-8|10-15"}
tc = load_timecourse()                              # the full long-form table
brca1 = tc[tc["gene"] == "BRCA1"]                   # filter to one gene

# sanity check: 5 rows, one per timepoint
brca1 = brca1.sort_values("time")                   # ensure x is monotonic

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 4.2))          # CREATE the canvas
ax.plot(brca1["time"], brca1["tpm"],                # CALL: x = time, y = tpm
        marker="o", color=COURSE_PAL[0], lw=2,      # green-teal "story" line
        markersize=6)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm")
ax.set_title("BRCA1 expression over 24h", color=INK)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
```
:::

## Time Series · Step 2 — All Six Genes {.smaller}

[Time series · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · One line per gene, distinct on-palette colours

Loop the six genes and draw one line per gene. The course palette covers five; for the sixth we use a neutral grey — a deliberate de-emphasis, the gene that doesn't compete for attention.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1-2|4-5|7-8|10-17|19-22"}
tc = load_timecourse()                                       # full long-form table
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]     # fixed order

# six colours: five course-palette + one neutral GREY for the last
palette = COURSE_PAL + [GREY]                                 # length-6 colour list

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.4))                    # CREATE the canvas

for gene, colour in zip(genes, palette):                      # one line per gene
    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")            # filter + order
    ax.plot(g["time"], g["tpm"],                              # CALL: trajectory
            marker="o", color=colour, lw=2,
            markersize=5, label=gene)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}

<!-- slide 20 -->
## Time Series · Step 3 — Error Bars {.smaller}

[Time series · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · `ax.errorbar` adds vertical whiskers at every point

Swap `ax.plot` for `ax.errorbar` and pass `yerr=g["sem"]`. The `capsize=3` gives the little horizontal caps that make whiskers readable. **Bracket access is mandatory** — `g.sem` is the method (slide 17).

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="10-16"}
tc = load_timecourse()
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]
palette = COURSE_PAL + [GREY]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.4))

for gene, colour in zip(genes, palette):
    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")

    # CALL: line + whiskers in one call. yerr=g["sem"], NOT g.sem
    ax.errorbar(g["time"], g["tpm"],
                yerr=g["sem"],                       # bracket access — sem is a column
                marker="o", color=colour, lw=2,
                markersize=5,
                capsize=3,                            # caps make whiskers readable
                label=gene)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm  (mean ± SEM)")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.4

tc = load_timecourse()
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.4))

for gene, colour in zip(genes, palette):
    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")
    ax.errorbar(g["time"], g["tpm"],
                yerr=g["sem"],
                marker="o", color=colour, lw=2,
                markersize=5,
                capsize=3,
                label=gene)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm  (mean ± SEM)")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::

<!-- slide 21 -->
## Time Series · Step 4 — Ribbons {.smaller}

[Time series · build]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · `ax.fill_between` replaces whiskers with a translucent envelope

When lines are dense, whiskers stack and clutter. Swap them for a **ribbon**: `ax.fill_between(time, tpm − sem, tpm + sem, alpha=0.25)`. The trajectory stays sharp; the uncertainty becomes a soft halo around it.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="10-14|16-19"}
tc = load_timecourse()
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]
palette = COURSE_PAL + [GREY]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.4))

for gene, colour in zip(genes, palette):
    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")

    # CALL 1: the trajectory line, sharp on top
    ax.plot(g["time"], g["tpm"],
            color=colour, lw=2, marker="o", markersize=5, label=gene)

    # CALL 2: the uncertainty ribbon, translucent below
    ax.fill_between(g["time"],
                    g["tpm"] - g["sem"],             # lower edge of the band
                    g["tpm"] + g["sem"],             # upper edge of the band
                    color=colour, alpha=0.20,        # see-through halo
                    linewidth=0)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm  (mean ± SEM)")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.4

                    g["tpm"] - g["sem"],
                    g["tpm"] + g["sem"],
                    color=colour, alpha=0.20,
                    linewidth=0)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)")
ax.set_ylabel("tpm  (mean ± SEM)")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
```

<!-- slide 22 -->
## Time Series · Step 5 — Small Multiples {.smaller}

[Time series · build]{.eyebrow}

### 5 · One panel per gene, faint grey context behind each focal trajectory

The killer plot. A 2×3 grid, **one gene per panel** in its colour with its SEM ribbon, and *every other gene drawn faintly in grey behind it* so each panel has full context. `sharex=True, sharey=True` keeps the axes comparable across panels.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1-3|5-9|11-18|20-25|27-31"}
tc = load_timecourse()
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]
palette = COURSE_PAL + [GREY]

# CREATE: 2 rows x 3 cols, shared axes for easy across-panel comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(8.4, 4.8),
                          sharex=True, sharey=True)
axes = axes.flatten()                                          # 6 axes, easy indexing

for ax, gene, colour in zip(axes, genes, palette):
    # context: every other gene as a faint grey line behind
    for other in genes:
        if other == gene:                                       # skip the focal
            continue
        o = tc[tc["gene"] == other].sort_values("time")
        ax.plot(o["time"], o["tpm"],
                color=LINE, lw=1, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)         # de-emphasised context

    # focal gene: full colour, ribbon, marker
    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")
    ax.plot(g["time"], g["tpm"], color=colour, lw=2.2,
            marker="o", markersize=4, zorder=3)                # on top of context
    ax.fill_between(g["time"], g["tpm"] - g["sem"], g["tpm"] + g["sem"],
                    color=colour, alpha=0.22, linewidth=0, zorder=2)

    ax.set_title(gene, color=colour, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

fig.supxlabel("time (hours)"); fig.supylabel("tpm")
plt.tight_layout()
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8.4
#| fig-height: 4.8

tc = load_timecourse()
genes = ["BRCA1", "TP53", "EGFR", "MYC", "KRAS", "PTEN"]
palette = COURSE_PAL + [GREY]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(8.4, 4.8),
                          sharex=True, sharey=True)
axes = axes.flatten()

for ax, gene, colour in zip(axes, genes, palette):
    for other in genes:
        if other == gene:
            continue
        o = tc[tc["gene"] == other].sort_values("time")
        ax.plot(o["time"], o["tpm"],
                color=LINE, lw=1, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)

    g = tc[tc["gene"] == gene].sort_values("time")
    ax.plot(g["time"], g["tpm"], color=colour, lw=2.2,
            marker="o", markersize=4, zorder=3)
    ax.fill_between(g["time"], g["tpm"] - g["sem"], g["tpm"] + g["sem"],
                    color=colour, alpha=0.22, linewidth=0, zorder=2)

    ax.set_title(gene, color=colour, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

fig.supxlabel("time (hours)"); fig.supylabel("tpm")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 23 -->
## Time Series · Seaborn Variant {.smaller}

[Time series · ergonomic]{.eyebrow}

### One `sns.lineplot` call replaces the loop

Seaborn understands long-form data natively. Pass the whole `tc` table, name the columns, and use `hue="gene"` — seaborn does the per-gene split, the colour cycling, *and* the standard-error ribbon (`errorbar="se"`) in one call. The cost: less control over each line's styling.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1|3-9|11-14"}
tc = load_timecourse()

# CALL: one line per `gene`, ribbon from `errorbar="se"`
ax = sns.lineplot(
    data=tc, x="time", y="tpm",
    hue="gene",                                       # split by gene -> 6 colours
    hue_order=["BRCA1","TP53","EGFR","MYC","KRAS","PTEN"],
    palette=COURSE_PAL + [GREY],                      # the same 6-colour list
    errorbar="se",                                    # ribbon = ± standard error
    marker="o", linewidth=2)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)"); ax.set_ylabel("tpm")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9, title="")
```

**Trade-off**: seaborn collapses the loop and adds a ribbon for free — perfect for **exploration**. matplotlib's explicit loop wins when you need **bespoke styling per line** (one bold, the rest dimmed; mixed dashes; small-multiples). Use seaborn to *see*, matplotlib to *publish*.
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.4

tc = load_timecourse()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.4))
sns.lineplot(
    data=tc, x="time", y="tpm",
    hue="gene",
    hue_order=["BRCA1","TP53","EGFR","MYC","KRAS","PTEN"],
    palette=COURSE_PAL + [GREY],
    errorbar="se",
    marker="o", linewidth=2,
    ax=ax)

ax.set_xlabel("time (hours)"); ax.set_ylabel("tpm")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
          frameon=False, fontsize=9, title="")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 24 -->
## Time Series · Takeaway {.smaller}

[Time series · recap]{.eyebrow}

### Trajectory plus uncertainty, scaled to your data

::: {.takeaway}
[The recipe]{.tl}
1. **Lines tell direction**, error bars or ribbons tell **confidence**.
2. **Error bars for few points** (≤ 6 timepoints); **ribbons for many**.
3. **Small multiples** isolate each story when lines overlap — keep faint grey context behind each panel.
4. **Always use bracket access** for `df["sem"]` — the dot-attribute collides with `DataFrame.sem()` and silently breaks.

Direction + confidence + isolation: the three knobs of every time-series figure. Pick the one your audience needs most for *this* plot.
:::
